name: Cambridge 15 Test 3 Task 1
prompt_text:
The diagram below shows how instant noodles are manufactured.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

notes: Eight stages in total.
extracted_data.title: Manufacturing instant noodles
process_steps: Storage silos: flour is delivered by truck and stored in silos.
Mixer: flour is mixed with water and oil.
Dough sheets: the dough is passed through rollers to make sheets.
Dough strips: the sheets are cut into strips.
Noodle discs: the strips are formed into discs.
Cooking (oil) + drying.
The noodles are put into cups and vegetables + spices are added.
Labelling + sealing: labels are added and the cups are sealed.

name: Cambridge 16 Test 2 Task 1
prompt_text:
The diagram below shows the manufacturing process for making sugar from sugar cane.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

notes: Seven stages in total.
extracted_data.title: How sugar is produced from sugar cane
process_steps: Growing: sugar canes grow for 12–18 months.
Harvesting: by machine or by hand.
Crushing: the sugar canes are crushed to extract juice.
Purifying juice: the juice passes through a limestone filter.
Evaporator: the juice is heated and becomes syrup.
Centrifuge: sugar crystals are separated from the syrup.
Drying and cooling: the sugar is dried and cooled.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

notes: Now: 8 gates, walkway, check-in and café in departures, nothing in arrivals hall.
extracted_data.title: Southwest Airport: now and after development
map_changes: The number of gates will increase from 8 (gates 1–8) to 18 (gates 1–18), arranged in a Y shape with two new branches to the north-west and north-east.
The walkway between the gates will be replaced by a sky train.
Shops will be added between the departures hall and the gates.
A bag drop will be added in the departures area next to check-in.
The café in departures will be moved to the bottom-left corner of the departures area.
In arrivals, a café, an ATM and a car hire facility will be added; the arrivals area will be extended with a small extension for car hire.
Unchanged: security and passport control in departures, passport control and customs in arrivals, check-in, and the departures and arrivals entrances.

name: Cambridge 16 Test 4 Task 1
prompt_text:
The diagram below shows the process for recycling plastic bottles.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

notes: The process is a cycle (nine stages).
extracted_data.title: How plastic bottles are recycled
process_steps: Plastic bottles are put into a recycling bin.
The bottles are collected by a truck.
Recycling centre: the bottles are sorted.
The bottles are compressed into blocks.
The blocks are crushed and then washed.
Plastic pellets are produced.
The pellets are heated to form raw material.
Raw material is produced.
End products are produced (e.g. bottles, food containers, clothing, bags, pens), which can then be recycled again.

extracted_data.title: Porth Harbour (in 2000) and Porth Harbour (today)
map_changes: The disused castle on the eastern headland has become a hotel.
The public beach on the south side of the headland is now a private beach for the hotel.
The dock now has an extra pier, so there is more space for passenger ferries.
The marina (private yachts) and fishing boats have swapped places: fishing boats are now in the northern basin and the marina is in the southern basin.
The southern car park has been reduced and a second showers & toilets block has been built next to it.
Cafés & shops have been built next to the lifeboat station on the road.
The road to the headland now has a roundabout leading to the hotel.
Unchanged: main road on the west, the northern showers & toilets and car park, the public beach in the north-east, the lifeboat station and passenger ferries.

name: Cambridge 19 Test 3 Task 1
prompt_text:
The diagram below shows how a biofuel called ethanol is produced.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

notes: Carbon dioxide is also released during harvesting and pre-processing.
The process is a cycle.
extracted_data.title: Biofuel production: how ethanol is made
process_steps: Plants and trees grow using energy (sunlight + carbon dioxide).
Harvesting (the crops and trees are cut and collected by machine).
Pre-processing (the plant material is broken down into small pieces).
Cellulose is produced.
Processing (in a laboratory / factory).
Sugars are produced.
Microbes are added.
Ethanol is produced.
Ethanol is used as fuel by cars, trucks and planes, which release carbon dioxide.
The carbon dioxide returns to the atmosphere and is used again by growing plants (cyclical process).
